source.title: Deep Linear Networks can Benignly Overfit when Shallow Ones Do
source.authors: Niladri S. Chatterji; Philip M. Long

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent and benign overfitting in related work, but its own results do not test the fall-rise-fall curves over model size, training time, or sample size, or the other specified versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own simulations measure excess risk under changes to initialization scale and input dimension, not the axes or mechanisms named in V1–V7. Those adjacent risk findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper bounds and simulates the excess risk of interpolating deep linear networks, always with d > n. Its simulations vary initialization scale and input dimension only within the overparameterized regime. No result shows a test-error curve over model size, epochs or samples crossing an interpolation threshold. Nothing tests effective complexity, noise-driven peaks or regularization removing a peak. Double descent appears only in the related-work appendix (A.1).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that interpolating deep linear networks have the same conditional variance as the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolant. Depth gives no benefit in their bounds or simulations; random initialization adds bias. The only way depth could help is if the initial function approximates the regression function.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and simulates excess risk for interpolating deep linear networks (and includes ReLU simulations), varying initialization and input dimension rather than sweeping model size, training time, or sample count as in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale changes excess risk in the linear experiments and with first-layer scaling in ReLU networks; the authors report that varying final-layer scale has little effect in the ReLU experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolating deep linear networks have exactly the same conditional variance as the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolant. Initialization adds only a bias term outside the data span. Depth therefore does not help 'hide the noise'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under squared loss, the harm from fitting noise in interpolating deep linear networks is independent of depth and initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Excess risk grows with first-layer initialization scale in linear and ReLU networks. It grows with last-layer scale in linear networks but is largely unaffected by it in ReLU networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale controls excess risk of interpolating networks, with layer-dependent asymmetry in ReLU networks.

record.problems: The simulation findings are presented in plots and described qualitatively in the text; the text does not give figure-specific numerical risk values. The simulations average 20 runs, and the theoretical bounds are upper bounds rather than lower bounds.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep across the interpolation threshold; width is tied to d and all runs interpolate.
No test risk over training time; only final interpolating solutions are evaluated.
n is fixed (100 or 500); no sample-size sweep.
Only the overparameterized regime (d > n) is studied; no underparameterized side and no peak.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak location; effective rank enters only the risk bounds.
Noise level and regularization are not varied; no peak to remove or split.

record.verdict_notes: Theory paper on benign overfitting, with simulations. Upper bounds only, no lower bounds. Its overparameterized-regime risk bounds are adjacent to the second-descent side of V4 but test no curve. The setup text reuses 'α' for the last-layer sweep, apparently a typo for β.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size or measurement of a peak near the interpolation threshold.
No test-error curve over training epochs or time.
No sweep of training sample count near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity-versus-risk double-descent curves across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across axes.
The paper does not test whether label noise or variance drives a double-descent peak, whether peaks split, or whether tuned regularization removes one.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters or test of whether that turns a second descent into an ordinary U shape.
